subject: Clarify HIPAA-aligned notification windows, evidence preservation & cooperation SLA
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@greenlinehealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Megan Park <megan@privacyconsults.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify notification windows & cooperative obligations for HIPAA-covered workloads

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Greenline is evaluating Redwood for an upcoming pilot that will process PHI, and our internal security/legal teams asked for a few clarifications around breach notification and cooperation language so we can proceed with a procurement timeline.

Specifically:
- Our InfoSec team needs to confirm what notification windows Redwood proposes after a confirmed security incident affecting customer-controlled PHI. We typically operate under HIPAA expectations and need clarity for contractual language.
- We also need to understand what evidence/data Redwood can provide (access logs, SIEM exports, packet capture is unlikely, but request timing). What are realistic delivery windows (initial scope, full logs)?
- Law enforcement delay requests: how do you handle requests to delay notification? Do you preserve evidence in a forensically-sound manner while balancing operational needs?

Attached is our security questionnaire (short). Can you confirm what you can commit to in a DPA/BAA and propose specific wording for:
  a) notification timing (e.g., initial notice within X hours of confirmation)
  b) preservation and escrow of logs for Y days
  c) cooperation steps and contact points (who coordinates with our incident response lead)

We'd like to include Redwood's standard position so our legal team can draft an initial redline. If we need to loop Legal or Sales, please do.

Best,
Sarah

--
Sarah Lewis
Security & Compliance Manager
Greenline Health

Attachments: Greenline_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify notification windows & cooperative obligations for HIPAA-covered workloads

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list, and for sharing the questionnaire. I'm copying Laura (sales) and Neha (privacy/legal) so we can surface our standard commitments and propose contract language. Below is our typical starting position for HIPAA/Breach-cooperation items; these are negotiable for enterprise/BAA customers.

1) Notification timing- Initial notification: we commit to notify the customer point of contact within 72 hours of confirming an incident that materially affects customer-controlled data.- Ongoing updates: we provide a preliminary incident summary within 72 hours and then daily updates for the first week or until contained.
2) Evidence & log delivery- What we can provide: access logs (authentication, API calls), runtime request metadata, server-side audit logs, and structured telemetry exports.- Delivery windows: initial scope (indicators, affected resource list) within 48 hours of request; bulk log exports on a best-effort basis within 10 business days depending on the scope and retention windows.- Redaction: we will redact internal operational fields and minimize PHI exposure in exports; we can provide guidance for redaction requirements to your team.
3) Preservation & escrow- We preserve relevant logs for 90 days by default; for customers with BAAs we can extend preservation windows via configuration or add-on retention.- For forensic preservation requests (e.g., law enforcement delay), we will preserve relevant data and place a preservation hold while we coordinate with legal — we will not delete or overwrite evidence unless instructed by the customer or a lawful order.
4) Law enforcement delays- We require written request from law enforcement and will follow applicable legal process. We will work with the customer to respect valid delay requests; however, we may disclose limited metadata to authorities as required by law.
5) Cooperation & contacts- Primary Redwood incident contact: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com (Incident Ops lead)- Legal privacy contact: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

I'll let Neha propose contract wording for a DPA/BAA. Laura, can you confirm if Greenline will need an accelerated SLA (shorter windows) tied to procurement?

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Security Lead
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify notification windows & cooperative obligations for HIPAA-covered workloads

Hi all — quick follow-up from Legal/Privacy. The bullet points below are proposed DPA/BAA clauses we can start from; these are intentionally concise so procurement has concrete language to redline.

A) Incident Notification- "Redwood will provide Customer with an initial written notification of any confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation. The initial notice will include: summary of the nature of the incident, affected resources, and preliminary mitigation steps."
B) Evidence Preservation- "Upon Customer request or as required by applicable law, Redwood will implement a preservation hold for relevant logs and artifacts and will not delete or overwrite preserved data for a minimum period of thirty (30) days. For BAAs, Redwood will extend preservation to ninety (90) days unless otherwise agreed in writing."
C) Log and Evidence Delivery- "Redwood will provide Customer with reasonable access to logs and evidence necessary for Customer to fulfill its regulatory obligations. Redwood will deliver an initial scope of affected resources and indicators within forty-eight (48) hours of request and make commercially reasonable efforts to produce full exports within ten (10) business days. If production of full exports will exceed this timeline, Redwood will notify Customer and provide a target delivery date."
D) Law Enforcement Delays- "Redwood will comply with valid law enforcement requests to delay notice and will notify the Customer of such requests unless prohibited by law; Redwood will preserve evidence pending resolution of the delay request."
E) Cooperation & Costs- "Redwood will reasonably cooperate with the Customer's incident response team, including designated points of contact and technical SMEs. Costs associated with extraordinary forensic work or long-term retention beyond the agreed preservation windows may be invoiced at Redwood's then-current professional services rates."

Notes: We intentionally avoid committing to immutable forensic preservation standards (e.g., full disk images) unless Greenline is under an enterprise contract with add-on for forensics. We can include tighter SLAs (48-hour initial notice, 30-day preservation) as part of a negotiated BAA/enterprise package.

Laura — please advise on procurement cadence. Sarah — happy to set up a brief call tomorrow with our incident ops + legal to walk through the clauses if helpful.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify notification windows & cooperative obligations for HIPAA-covered workloads

Thanks Neha — that draft language is very helpful and much clearer than the questionnaire alone. A couple of follow-ups from Greenline legal & our DPO: 
- We'd like the preservation clause set to 90 days for PHI incidents by default in the BAA (Greenline cannot accept 30-day default for PHI). Can Redwood confirm that's possible as an SLA for healthcare customers?
- We will need explicit BAA language stating responsibilities for notifying affected individuals vs customer obligations; our usual approach is that the customer (covered entity) is responsible for patient notifications but requires vendor cooperation and timely evidence sharing. Please add a clause to reflect that split of responsibilities.
- For log exports that contain PHI, Greenline requests a certified delivery mechanism (SFTP with encryption or secure Drive link) and a maximum window of 5 business days for initial logs once a preservation hold is placed.

If Redwood can accept baseline 90-day preservation for PHI and 5-day initial log delivery for incidents impacting PHI, we can move forward with procurement and Laura can send the PO. If those need further commercial discussion, please escalate to Sales.

Appreciate the prompt responses — happy to jump on a 30-minute call if easier.

Best,
Sarah Lewis
Security & Compliance Manager
Greenline Health
